title: How a Hard Drive Works in 60 Seconds 💽🧲 #shorts
description:
A hard drive stores your files as tiny magnetic patches on spinning metal platters. A read/write head floats just nanometers above the surface on a cushion of air, flipping or sensing north and south magnetic regions that mean 1 and 0, while a magnet-driven arm swings it to the right track. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#harddrive #hdd #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Inside many hard drives, metal platters spin *7,200 times* every minute.

steps.label: Platters
steps.text: Each *platter* is coated with a thin *magnetic* layer.

steps.label: Head
steps.text: A tiny *head* floats just *nanometers* above it, riding a cushion of air.

steps.label: Bits
steps.text: Your data is millions of *magnetized* patches. North or south means *1 or 0*.

steps.label: Arm
steps.text: A *magnet-driven arm* swings the head to the right *track* in milliseconds.

steps.label: Read
steps.text: To read, the head *senses* each patch's field and turns it into a *signal*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, float, *magnetize*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
